children: Hawaiian Electric Industries monetized 30% of its 9.9% stake in American Savings Bank, a move the company said will strengthen its financial position and reduce its financing needs for future wildfire settlement payments.
The sale came as part of ASB's initial public offering, Hawaiian Electric said Monday.

Hawaiian Electric sold roughly 2 million shares, resulting in $29.5 million in proceeds, net of underwriting fees and issuance costs. Underwriters will have 30 days to purchase up to nearly 294,000 additional shares from Hawaiian Electric, which would result in an additional $4.4 million in net proceeds.

Following the sale, Hawaiian Electric has a remaining 6.4% stake in ASB, valued at roughly $73.5 million. The company said it will consider plans to monetize its remaining shares following the expiration of a 180-day lockup period, subject to market conditions and other relevant considerations.
Proceeds from the sale will reduce future capital raises required for the remaining Maui wildfire settlement payments, Hawaiian Electric said.
